A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding methods, proofs, and experiments can be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic subspace-recovery, image colorization and denoising, and speech classification experiments in Section 4 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E and adds automatic speech intelligibility and quality measurements.

M1.justification: v1's mix-and-match objective conditions on observed style G. v2's multi-view formulation learns both content and style encoders and adds the cross-view information penalty I(Ghat1;X2) in Equation 8. Section 4.3 also specifies a multi-view subspace adaptation with content guidance. The original image style-guidance objective is retained.

E1.justification: Both evaluate latent-subspace GMM recovery, MNIST colorization, CIFAR10 color-shift denoising, and voice-conversion adaptation on IEMOCAP, ADReSS, and ALS-TDI. The expanded multi-view theory does not add an evaluated dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain unregularized image models and the same speech comparators: No VC, pitch shifting, KNN-VC, TriAAN-VC, and Diff-VC. Newly mentioned whisper-large-v2 and UTMOS are evaluation tools, not additional competing conversion methods.

E3.justification: v2 Table 6 adds WER measured with whisper-large-v2 and predicted MOS measured with UTMOS to the existing IEMOCAP evaluation. The documented training budgets, architectures, data splits, cross-validation, and previous metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The style-guidance ablations, noise-scheduler and sample-size sweeps, target-speaker-count analysis, and qualitative image examples are retained. The new WER/MOS columns add performance metrics without a separate ablation, robustness test, or diagnostic study.

E5.justification: Four synthetic trials, two image trials, and existing uncertainty displays are retained. However, v1 Section 4 specifies four randomly selected speaker combinations per target-speaker count; v2 omits this repetition detail. Its generic checklist statement about multiple runs does not establish any change in actual repetitions.

E6.justification: All previous numerical table entries are retained. v2 Table 6 adds ten WER/MOS values across five speech methods: for example, Diff-VC reports 22.9 WER and 2.5 MOS, versus 9.0 and 2.3 for No VC. These are newly reported measurements, not improvements over v1's unchanged classification scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds information retention to disentanglement and replaces the earlier deterministic editability definition with conditional stochastic generation. It revises assumptions, multi-view guarantees, and finite-sample editability derivations, and adds correlated-factor extensions in B.7 and C.4. Much subspace/NTK theory is retained in Appendix D. The revised B.2 argument also introduces an invalid general triangle inequality for KL divergence.

C1.justification: The contribution is expanded from observed-style recovery and augmentation to recovering content/style encodings under partial-label or multi-view supervision, using explicit information-retention and stochastic-editability criteria. The abstract and conclusion emphasize this revised scope. Style guidance and finite-sample convergence were already contributions in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of multi-view information loss, the role of style-information regularization, sensitivity to nearly degenerate subspaces, and difficulties with correlated factors or limited data. It explicitly limits empirical validation to controlled settings. The earlier content-distortion warning and speech-domain-mismatch discussion are retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the models used for the new WER/MOS measurements and adds a commitment to release code and data upon acceptance. This is not evidence of an actual release. Existing architecture, optimizer, hardware, timing, and pretrained-checkpoint details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around nonlinear ICA, independent subspace analysis, weak supervision, and multi-view identifiability, including von Kügelgen et al., Daunhawer et al., and Yao et al. It also broadens diffusion-theory coverage and contrasts its stochastic observation setting with prior invertible formulations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, and related work are extensively rewritten. Diffusion background precedes the problem formulation, theoretical subsections gain Overview and Intuition passages, and proof appendices are consolidated and reordered. v2 also adds a contents page and conference checklist.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redesigned to show two supervision settings; v1 Figures 4–5 are merged into v2 Figure 3; plots receive revised markers, legends, and labels; and the IEMOCAP table gains WER/MOS columns. Appendix displays are extensively repositioned, while the image examples themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves conceptual organization, explicitly distinguishes independence from information retention, and adds useful speech-quality evidence. However, its rewritten Appendix B.2 replaces v1's bounding argument with an invalid general KL-divergence triangle inequality, creating a material proof gap supporting Theorem 4.1. These benefits coexist with weakened theoretical support; the PDFs do not establish whether the broader guarantees survive correction, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
